Bug_Title: EI: May expose internal representation by returning a buffer sharing non-public data (EI_EXPOSE_BUF)
Bug_Details:
Returning a reference to a buffer (java.nio.*Buffer) which wraps an array stored in one of the object's fields
exposes the internal representation of the array elements because the buffer only stores a reference to the array
instead of copying its content. Similarly, returning a shallow-copy of such a buffer (using its duplicate() method)
stored in one of the object's fields also exposes the internal representation of the buffer. 
 If instances are accessed by untrusted code, and unchecked changes to
 the array would compromise security or other
 important properties, you will need to do something different.
Returning a read-only buffer (using its asReadOnly() method) or copying the array to a new buffer (using its put()
method) is a better approach in many situations.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the getBuffer method, which returns an IntBuffer that wraps the private data array. This allows external code to modify the internal state of the object through the returned buffer.
Trigger_Explanation: The test calls the showBug method, which internally uses the getBuffer method. The getBuffer method returns an IntBuffer that wraps the private data array. Modifying the original data array affects the contents of the buffer, demonstrating that the internal representation is exposed.
Test_Run_Result:
JUnit version 4.13.2
.Buffer contents before modification:
10 20 30 40 50 
Buffer contents after modification:
999 20 30 40 50 

Time: 0.01

OK (1 test)
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm that modifying the original data array affects the contents of the buffer returned by the getBuffer() method. Before modification, the buffer contains the values [10, 20, 30, 40, 50], and after modifying the first element of the original data array to 999, the buffer reflects this change, showing [999, 20, 30, 40, 50]. This demonstrates that the buffer shares the same underlying array as the original data, confirming the bug.
